html:
This bar covers the independent nations of Southeast Asia after colonial rule, from the declarations of Indonesia and Vietnam in 1945 to the present. Today the region has eleven states and close to 700 million people.

Japan's conquest of the region in 1942 broke the hold of European colonial rule, and when Japan surrendered in August 1945, nationalists moved fast. Independence came in different ways:

  • By declaration and war: Sukarno declared Indonesia independent in August 1945 and fought the Dutch until 1949. Hồ Chí Minh declared Vietnam independent in September 1945 and fought France until 1954.
  • By negotiation: the Philippines from the United States in 1946, Burma from Britain in 1948, Malaya in 1957.
  • By merger and split: Malaysia formed in 1963, and Singapore left it in 1965 under Lee Kuan Yew.
  • Cambodia and Laos became independent from France in 1953, and Brunei and East Timor came later.

The decades after brought war and dictatorship. The Vietnam War spread to Laos and Cambodia, where Pol Pot's Khmer Rouge killed perhaps a quarter of the population from 1975 to 1979. Military and strongman rule took hold under Suharto in Indonesia, Marcos in the Philippines and the generals in Burma.

From the 1970s much of the region turned to export industry and grew fast, from Singapore and Malaysia to Thailand and, after reforms in 1986, Vietnam. ASEAN, founded in 1967 by five anti-communist states, grew to take in every state of the region, the last being East Timor in 2025. Democracy has advanced and retreated by turns, from the fall of Marcos in 1986 to Myanmar's coup in 2021.
sum: This bar covers the independent nations of Southeast Asia after colonial rule, from the declarations of Indonesia and Vietnam in 1945 to the present. Today the region has eleven states and close to 700 million people.
